title: Into the Woods
tagline: Bread from the baker, beans from Jack, and a pie for Granny.
about: A childless baker and his wife set off into the forest to lift a witch's curse, crossing paths with Cinderella, Little Red Riding Hood, Jack and Rapunzel.
cue: Serve the snacks when Little Red Riding Hood turns up at the bakery and fills her basket.
faces: OPEN LATE. MIND THE QUIET CORNER
At the edge of the forest. Bread baked daily.
Gone to the forest with your father's old jacket. The dough is proving, the oven is lit, and do not let Red walk off with the whole basket again.
Six stamps for a free loaf. Ten stamps. Nobody remembers the tenth.

    StartersLittle Red's basket cheese and herb bunsSoft pull-apart bread buns with cheddar, chives and thyme, baked golden with a melted cheese topHow to make it500g bread flour7g dried yeast1 tsp caster sugar1 tsp salt300ml warm milk40g butter, softened150g cheddar, grated2 tbsp chives, chopped1 tsp thyme leaves1 egg, beatenMix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, warm milk and butter and knead for 10 minutes until smooth. Knead in two thirds of the cheddar with the chives and thyme.Cover and prove until doubled.Divide into 12 and roll into tight balls. Set them close together in a lined 23cm square tin.Cover and prove until puffy and touching. Heat the oven to 200°C.Brush with the egg, scatter with the rest of the cheddar and bake until golden.Cool for 10 minutes, then pull apart into a cloth-lined basket.Jack's cow-for-beans broad bean crostiniToasted baguette with ricotta and bright crushed broad beans, mint, garlic and lemonHow to make it500g frozen broad beans1 garlic clove, crushed1 lemon, zested and juiced2 tbsp mint, chopped80ml extra virgin olive oilsalt and pepper, to taste1 baguette, in 1cm slices150g ricottaCook the broad beans in boiling water for 3 minutes, drain and cool in cold water.Pop the bright green beans out of their pale skins.Crush roughly with the garlic, lemon zest and juice, mint and half the oil, and season with salt and pepper.Brush the baguette slices with the rest of the oil and toast under the grill until golden.Spread each toast with ricotta and pile on the crushed beans.Roast pumpkin and sage pastiesFor the two princes, still in agony.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsGranny's cottage chicken and mushroom pot pieChicken thigh, leek, mushrooms and thyme in a creamy mustard sauce under a deep golden puff pastry lidHow to make it800g boneless chicken thighs, in 3cm pieces30g butter1 tbsp vegetable oil1 leek, sliced250g button mushrooms, halved2 garlic cloves, crushed3 sprigs of thyme, leaves picked3 tbsp plain flour400ml chicken stock150ml thickened cream1 tsp Dijon mustard2 tbsp parsley, choppedsalt and pepper, to taste2 sheets of frozen puff pastry, thawed1 egg, beatenSeason the chicken and brown it in the butter and oil in a large frying pan. Lift out.Soften the leek, button mushrooms, garlic and thyme in the same pan.Stir in the flour, then the stock, cream and mustard. Return the browned filling and simmer until thick.Stir in the parsley, season and spoon into a 2 litre pie dish. Cool for 10 minutes.Heat the oven to 200°C. Lay the pastry over the top, overlapping the sheets, trim and press the edges, brush with the egg and cut a small steam hole.Bake until puffed and deep golden.Rest for 5 minutes before serving.King's festival roast pork with applesThree nights of the King's festival, and Cinderella runs out of every oneHow to make it1.5kg pork loin, skin on1 tbsp sea salt flakes4 apples2 brown onions1 sage250ml cloudy apple juice1 tbsp plain flour300g green beans200g baby spinach20g butterHeat the oven to 240°C. Score the skin, rub with the salt and sit the pork on the quartered apples, onions and sage in a roasting tin.Roast for 30 minutes until the skin crackles, then turn down to 180°C.Roast for 1 more hour, then rest for 15 minutes.Stir the flour into the pan juices on the stove, add the apple juice and simmer for 4 minutes for gravy.Boil the beans for 4 minutes, then toss with the spinach and butter until wilted.Carve and serve with the roast apples, gravy and greens.SweetsRapunzel's golden apple plaitSoft buttery sweet bread twisted into a long plait around cinnamon apple, glazed with honey, with whipped creamHow to make it400g bread flour7g dried yeast50g caster sugar1/2 tsp salt150ml warm milk2 eggs80g butter, softened, for the dough30g butter, softened, for the filling60g brown sugar1 tsp ground cinnamon2 green apples, peeled and grated2 tbsp honey200ml thickened creamMix the flour, yeast, caster sugar, salt, warm milk and eggs, then knead in the dough butter bit by bit until smooth and glossy.Cover and prove until doubled.Squeeze the apple dry. Roll the dough out to 40cm by 30cm, spread with the filling butter and scatter with the brown sugar, cinnamon and apple.Roll up from a long side, cut in half lengthways and twist the two strands together, cut sides up, into a long plait. Set on a lined tray.Cover loosely and prove until puffy. Heat the oven to 180°C.Bake until deep golden and cooked through.Brush with the warmed honey, cool a little and serve in slices with the cream, lightly whipped.DrinksMilky White's vanilla milkshakeThick, frothy cold milk blended with vanilla ice cream, vanilla and a little honey, dusted with nutmegHow to make it800ml cold milk6 scoops of vanilla ice cream1 tsp vanilla extract1 tbsp honeypinch of ground nutmegBlend the milk, ice cream, vanilla and honey until thick and frothy.Pour into 4 tall chilled glasses.Dust each with a pinch of nutmeg and serve with a straw.Fresh pressed pear juiceInto the woods, and home before dark.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
